title: ESP32 CYD Android OS - Lua App Development Toolkit

target_hardware.mcu: ESP32-D0WD-V3 (Dual Core Tensilica LX6 @ 240MHz, 520KB SRAM, 4MB Flash)

touch.bus: VSPI (or HSPI shared with soft CS)
touch.filtering: Hardware HAL provides 3-sample median filter, jitter rejection, and debounce

peripherals.rgb_led: Active-LOW RGB pins on board, controlled via sys.setLED(r, g, b)
peripherals.buzzer: Piezo speaker on GPIO 26, controlled via sys.beep(freq, dur)
peripherals.ldr: Light Dependent Resistor on GPIO 34 (ADC1), read via sys.getLdr()
peripherals.sd_card: MicroSD slot on VSPI (CS pin GPIO 5, FAT32 formatted)

runtime_environment.heap_budget: ~100KB to 160KB RAM available for Lua VM and scripts
runtime_environment.execution_model: Synchronous single-threaded UI loop with cooperative multitasking
runtime_environment.os_shell_pumping: sys.delay(ms) and an instruction count hook (1000 instructions) automatically pump the OS touch router, status bar, and navigation bar
runtime_environment.exit_mechanism: Pressing the Navigation Bar Back or Home button sets an internal abort flag and throws an abort exception, cleanly returning to the Launcher

system_status_bar.ownership: Reserved exclusively for the OS shell (shows time, battery, RAM, SD status)
system_status_bar.rule: Apps MUST NEVER draw within Y < 20

app_viewport.rule: ALL portrait application visuals and touch interaction MUST stay strictly within this 240x274 rectangle

system_nav_bar.ownership: Reserved exclusively for OS Navigation (< Back, O Home, [] Tasks)
system_nav_bar.rule: Apps MUST NEVER draw within Y >= 294 and should avoid placing touch buttons below Y = 285

landscape_compatibility_mode.description: The OS includes an automatic Landscape Compatibility Layer. If a Lua script declares `-- @orientation: landscape`, calls `sys.setOrientation('landscape')`, or uses legacy `VP_W = 320` / `VP_H = 194` / `320, 194` dimensions, the OS automatically rotates the display, touch digitizer, StatusBar, and NavBar to Landscape (320x240) while the app runs, and restores Portrait (240x320) on exit.

font_1.recommended_use: Compact data, terminal logs, small labels, hex data

font_2.recommended_use: Standard UI buttons, lists, titles, values, dialogs (Default font)

font_4.recommended_use: Big clock display, calculator readout, prominent counters

app_design_rules.rule: Never draw over System Status Bar or Nav Bar
app_design_rules.detail: Always keep visual boundaries within X: 0 to 239, Y: 20 to 293. Drawing outside clutters OS components.
Call `sys.delay(15)` to `sys.delay(30)` in every iteration of your app_main loop. Without this, the watchdog will panic or the Back/Home buttons won't respond.
Never call full-screen clears inside the main touch loop. Paint the full UI once on startup, then redraw only the specific rectangles/buttons that change state.
Resistive touch screens produce continuous 'true' while pressed. Track `wasPressed` to detect a fresh press (DOWN) versus continuous drag versus release (UP).
Include a subtle audio beep `sys.beep(1200, 15)` and momentary button highlight when a user interacts with a touch target.
Avoid repeatedly concatenating large strings or allocating temporary tables inside 30-fps render loops to prevent GC pauses.

hello_world_portrait.title: Minimal Portrait App (240x274 Default Viewport)
hello_world_portrait.lua_code:
-- Minimal CYD Portrait Lua App
-- @orientation: portrait
local VP_X, VP_Y, VP_W, VP_H = 0, 20, 240, 274

gui.fillRect(VP_X, VP_Y, VP_W, VP_H, 0x0821)
gui.fillRect(12, VP_Y + 16, 216, 140, 0x18E3)
gui.drawRect(12, VP_Y + 16, 216, 140, 0x39E7)

gui.drawText(24, VP_Y + 28, "Hello CYD Portrait!", 0x07FF, 2)
gui.drawText(24, VP_Y + 54, "240x320 Vertical Mode", 0xFFFF, 1)

local count = 0
local lastPressed = false

while true do
    local tx, ty, pressed = input.getTouch()
    if pressed and not lastPressed then
        if tx >= 12 and tx <= 228 and ty >= (VP_Y + 16) and ty <= (VP_Y + 156) then
            count = count + 1
            sys.beep(1500, 15)
            gui.fillRect(24, VP_Y + 80, 190, 20, 0x18E3)
            gui.drawText(24, VP_Y + 80, "Taps: " .. count .. " | Heap: " .. sys.getHeap() .. "B", 0x07E0, 1)
        end
        lastPressed = true
    elseif not pressed and lastPressed then
        lastPressed = false
    end
    sys.delay(20)
end

custom_touch_button_pattern.title: Clean Reusable Button Handler Pattern
custom_touch_button_pattern.lua_code:
local buttons = {
    { id = "btn1", x = 20,  y = 60, w = 130, h = 40, label = "ENABLE",  color = 0x04F5 },
    { id = "btn2", x = 170, y = 60, w = 130, h = 40, label = "DISABLE", color = 0x4208 }
}

local function drawButton(b, isPressed)
    local bg = isPressed and 0xFFFF or b.color
    local fg = isPressed and 0x0000 or 0xFFFF
    gui.fillRect(b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h, bg)
    gui.drawRect(b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h, 0x0000)
    local tx = b.x + math.floor((b.w - (#b.label * 8)) / 2)
    local ty = b.y + math.floor((b.h - 16) / 2)
    gui.drawText(tx, ty, b.label, fg, 2)
end

-- Initial render
for _, b in ipairs(buttons) do drawButton(b, false) end

local activeBtn = nil
while true do
    local tx, ty, touched = input.getTouch()
    if touched then
        for _, b in ipairs(buttons) do
            if tx >= b.x and tx <= (b.x + b.w) and ty >= b.y and ty <= (b.y + b.h) then
                if activeBtn ~= b.id then
                    activeBtn = b.id
                    drawButton(b, true)
                    sys.beep(1200, 20)
                    -- Perform button action here
                end
            end
        end
    else
        if activeBtn then
            for _, b in ipairs(buttons) do
                if b.id == activeBtn then drawButton(b, false) end
            end
            activeBtn = nil
        end
    end
    sys.delay(20)
end

sd_card_app_launcher.title: Dynamic SD Card File Reader & App Launcher
sd_card_app_launcher.lua_code:
local VP_Y = 20
gui.fillRect(0, VP_Y, 320, 194, 0x0821)
gui.drawText(10, VP_Y + 10, "SD Card Apps Explorer", 0x07FF, 2)

if not sys.isSDMounted() then
    sys.probeSD()
end

local files = file.list("/sd")
local yOffset = VP_Y + 36
for i, f in ipairs(files) do
    if f.isLua and i <= 5 then
        gui.fillRect(10, yOffset, 300, 26, 0x18E3)
        gui.drawRect(10, yOffset, 300, 26, 0x39E7)
        gui.drawText(16, yOffset + 5, f.name .. " (" .. f.size .. "B)", 0xFFFF, 2)
        yOffset = yOffset + 30
    end
end

while true do
    local tx, ty, pressed = input.getTouch()
    if pressed then
        local index = math.floor((ty - (VP_Y + 36)) / 30) + 1
        if index >= 1 and index <= #files and files[index].isLua then
            sys.beep(1600, 40)
            -- Launch the selected app dynamically into the OS
            sys.launch(files[index].path)
            break
        end
    end
    sys.delay(25)
end

storage_options.hot_reload: True. Place script on FAT32 MicroSD card, insert into CYD, open 'Files' app, tap script, and press '> RUN LUA APP'. No reflash needed.
Persisted on LittleFS. Can be written via file.write() from Lua IDE / Terminal, or bundled into data/apps/

debugging_tips: If a script throws a runtime or syntax error, the OS catches it and renders a red 'Script error' screen with the exact line number and error message.
Always call sys.delay(ms) in loops so the user can press the hardware Nav Bar Home or Back button to exit safely back to the launcher.
